To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the semantic structure of the verb is reflected in the syntactic structure of the sentence; 2) semantic structure theory can explain the distribution of thematic roles in the verb phrase; 3) semantic structure theory is also useful for explaining why certain thematic roles are not found in the verb phrase, and why certain thematic roles occur in certain verb phrases but not others;
the mental lexicon is organized around the notion of meaning; that lexical relations are important for language learning; and that lexical semantics is relevant to language teaching.

the semantic relations between verbs are more important than the semantic features that verbs have in common with other verbs; that the semantic features of verbs are more important in determining their syntactic properties than the semantic features of other verbs; and that the semantic features that determine the syntax of verbs are more relevant to second language learners than semantic relations between verbs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between lexical meaning, syntactic structure, and language use in the second language classroom.
the nature of lexical semantics and the ways in which it is manifested in language use.
how the lexicon of the second language learner is acquired, organized, and used in the context of language production and processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lexical semantics research has contributed a great deal to the understanding of how words are stored and processed in the mental lexicon and how they are organized into semantic networks.
the lexical semantics research is a very complex and difficult field, which is not yet well established and understood.

the lexical semantics of a language is a complex system of interrelated semantic relations and that the semantic relations between lexical items are the key to understanding the lexical semantics of the language.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lexical semantic research is concerned with the meaning and structure of words, and the ways in which words are related to one another and to the grammar of the language.

we have demonstrated how the study of lexical semantics can be used as an instrument for the study of the acquisition of a new language, and how it can be used as a tool for the development of a new language.
lexical semantics is a field of study that is still in its infancy and has much to offer in terms of theoretical advances and practical applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

language learning and language use are not simply matters of acquiring and using the right words in the right way; they involve a complex set of interactions between lexical semantics, syntax, and pragmatics.
lexical semantics is a complex area of research that is of central importance to second language acquisition and pedagogy.

the lexical semantic knowledge of second language speakers can be significantly improved through the use of carefully designed tasks and materials that are grounded in the principles of semantic transfer.
